details:
We developed a prototype for a 2D planetary rover mission-design game inspired by NASA's Mars exploration missions, particularly Opportunity's investigation of ancient water at Meridiani Planum. The game is designed to guide players through the process of planning and designing a scientific exploration mission, beginning with a mission briefing followed by rover design. Players will select rover components while balancing engineering constraints such as mass, budget, power, and scientific instrument capabilities. The planned exploration stage will allow players to explore and investigate geological features and collect scientific evidence before evaluating their mission results.

This project aims to make complex concepts in aerospace engineering and planetary exploration more accessible and engaging for learners with limited prior experience through interactive learning. It encourages scientific curiosity while introducing players to the relationship between engineering decisions and scientific discoveries.

We developed the project's 2D environment and front-end prototype using GDevelop and its event-based programming system. The current prototype includes the main menu, mission briefing, and rover engineering interface, while the interactive gameplay systems remain a work in progress.

This project's creative approach lies in connecting rover engineering with real-world scientific investigations rather than creating a generic planetary exploration game. During development, we considered scientific accuracy, educational value, and engineering trade-offs, including mass, budget, power requirements, and instrument capabilities. Our intended impact is to inspire interest in planetary science, space engineering, and STEM.
